Subject: Tenant data routing / locality confirmations for Dedicated instance

Hi Marcus / Laura,

Thanks for taking the call earlier. We want to capture a concise checklist for our security and legal teams to confirm how tenant data will be pinned and removed in the Dedicated deployment we're evaluating. A few concrete asks: 

- Can you confirm that write and primary serving traffic for our tenant will be anchored to the us-west-2 region and will not be replicated to other regions by default?
- What are the default snapshot/backup retention windows for Dedicated (hot snapshots, warm backups, long-term archives)?
- In the event of a customer-requested deletion, what is the end-to-end timeline for removal from all live caches, snapshots, and cold backups?
- Are ephemeral KV caches and prefix caches tenant-scoped and cleared on erase?

I've attached a quick diagram and a spreadsheet with our expected retention window to help orient the asks. Please send a short runbook or bullet answers we can include in our SOC/attestation package.

Alex

Alex — thanks for the clear list. Pulling together concise answers below; I copied Ben and Laura for ops/backup details. High-level summary first, then specifics.

High level:
- Primary tenant serving and persistent storage can be anchored to a single region (us-west-2) for Dedicated customers. We do not replicate live tenant data to other regions unless replication is explicitly enabled in your config or required for a signed DR agreement.
- Backups/snaps: hot snapshots (for quick restores) are retained for 7 days by default; warm backups for 30 days; long-term archived backups are user-configurable with export — default: 90 days. We can negotiate different retention windows in the contract.
- Deletion timeline: we have a multi-stage purge: live caches evicted immediately on request, snapshots marked for deletion within 24 hours, and physical removal from cold storage depends on the archive provider's lifecycle (typically up to 30 days).

I'll let Ben add exact operational steps and the checklist items you can drop into your SOC pack.

—Marcus
Marcus Lin

Alex — adding the ops checklist and specifics you can paste into the SOW / security pack. I'll keep this in bullets for copy-paste.

Operational checklist (tenant-scoped routing & deletion):

1) Region pinning
- Tenant config: region_pin = "us-west-2" (applies to primary serving endpoints and persistent object store).
- Smart routing: control-plane policy prevents cross-region scheduling for tenant workloads unless an override flag (region_burst: true) is set by the customer and signed off.

2) Replication behavior
- No cross-region live replication by default.
- Snapshots are stored in region-by-default primary buckets; cross-region replication only if snapshot_replication_enabled = true.

3) Cache eviction and KV stores
- In-memory prefix caches and KV caches are tenant-scoped on Dedicated and are cleared synchronously when a delete request is processed.
- We issue a CacheInvalidate RPC to all serving nodes for the tenant; acknowledgement is awaited from the routing layer (typical < 5s).

4) Snapshot/backups and retention
- Hot snapshots: incremental delta snapshots every 6 hours, retained 7 days.
- Warm backups: daily full snapshot, rotated 30 days.
- Archive exports: optional export to customer-managed storage with retention controlled by customer policy (default 90 days).

5) Deletion workflow (customer-initiated ERASE request)
- Step 1 (T+0): Accept ERASE request via support API; mark tenant as deletion_in_progress.
- Step 2 (T+0–T+1): Invalidate live caches and suspend new writes.
- Step 3 (T+1–T+24): Mark snapshots and backups for deletion; prevent snapshot read access.
- Step 4 (T+24–T+720): Physical deletion from cloud object storage depends on provider — Redwood will persist deletion markers and will request garbage collection; typical window up to 30 days.

6) Evidence & attestation
- We provide a signed deletion ticket and an operation log (obfuscated token-level data) showing cache invalidations, snapshot deletion markers, and final object deletion requests.

7) Exceptions / legal holds
- If a legal hold is in place, deletion will be paused until clearance; retention policy will reflect holds.

If these timelines are acceptable, we can convert the above into an SOW paragraph and a one-page runbook.

Priya — quick answers below so your legal/compliance can move forward.

- CMK encryption: Yes. Warm backups and archive exports can be encrypted with your customer-managed KMS keys. We'll surface the key ARN in the SOW and include key rotation considerations.
- Proof artifacts: Yes. At T+24 we provide a deletion ticket and a list of object IDs and cloud delete request IDs. We can format these into a CSV or include them in a signed attestation PDF.

Action items: 
- Ben: produce a one-page runbook from the checklist and a sample deletion ticket template.
- Laura: include the CMK key ARN field in the onboarding template and flag the SOW clause for encryption.
- Alex/Priya: confirm whether you want archive exports enabled by default or controlled via separate request.

I'll follow up with the draft runbook early next week.
